summary.text: An 85-year-old man with diabetes for three years, treated with metformin and glipizide, left a hospital at his request two days before presenting to nephrology with bilateral pedal edema and oliguria for two days. At that hospital he had been treated for upper gastrointestinal bleeding with hematemesis and melena, was given a transfusion, and a gastric ulcer found on endoscopy was treated with proton pump inhibitors. He preferred a liquid diet for a week.

At the previous hospital creatinine rose from 1.12 mg/dL on admission to a peak of 5.43 mg/dL on the 11th day. Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal-sized kidneys with slightly increased echoes and no features of obstruction. On admission to the nephrology hospital he denied painkillers or native medications and dialysis was started. Urinalysis showed 1+ proteinuria and a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 1.8, with negative viral serologies and ANCA and normal complement levels.

Kidney biopsy showed crystals in about 20-25% of tubules, birefringent under polarized light, with tubular epithelial cell injury and three of 11 glomeruli globally sclerotic, giving biopsy-proven oxalate nephropathy with acute kidney injury. Repeat CT showed no nephrocalcinosis and 24-hour urine oxalate was 13.57 mg. On questioning he had taken pomegranate juice three to four times daily, and sometimes sweet lime juice, for a week.

He was advised a low oxalate diet and to avoid juices and was started on Oxalobacter formigenes capsules twice daily. After two weeks on dialysis he failed to attend dialysis and was lost to follow-up, so his later kidney recovery is not known.
